README.html.title: Fanex.Data - A Dapper-based data access library with configurable stored procedure names. | Fanex.Data
README.html.summary: Fanex.Data - A Dapper-based data access library with configurable stored procedure names. Packages Fanex.Data 4.3.4.5 Fanex.Data.Repository 4.3.4.5 Fanex.Data.MySql 4.3.4.5 Fanex.Data.SqlServer 4.3.4.5 Package Purposes: Fanex.Data The core library simplifies data access by leveraging Dapper. It centrally manages stored procedure names and connections through configuration files. Fanex.Data.Repository Introduces the DynamicRepository class, a simplified wrapper for Fanex.Data's ObjectDb. It provides a more straightforward interface for basic database operations, making it an ideal choice for quick and simple data access needs. Fanex.Data.MySql The MySQL-specific implementation of the Fanex.Data library Fanex.Data.SqlServer The SqlServer-specific implementation of the Fanex.Data library Features Fanex.Data is a lightweight data access library built on top of Dapper, extending its capabilities with configurable stored procedure names via an SpNames.xml file. This key feature is especially useful for managing different versions of stored procedures, allowing you to easily configure your application to call specific versions like xtest, xpre, or UAT stored procedures, even within a production environment. By centralizing the configuration of stored procedure names, Fanex.Data improves maintainability and provides a flexible solution for both SQL Server and MySQL, all while leveraging Dapper's high performance and simplicity. Key Features Features Execute a stored procedure returning data sets then map them to strongly typed lists. Extend ADO.Net CRUD functionalities working with stored procedures. Anonymous objects, strongly type objects, or IDictionary typed objects can be used as parameter sets to set values to stored procedure's parameters. Automatically assign values of OUTPUT parameters back to the parameter sets; which can be anonymous objects, strongly type objects, or IDictionary typed objects. Wrap any exception occurred with diagnostic information, such as: stored procedure name, parameters which are used in the execution, connection string, etc. Avoid throwing exceptions if number of values does not meet number of parameters listed in stored procedure definition. Allow developers to: Configure connection strings and connection aliases. Map between columns of result set and objects' properties. Define firm parameters, parameters which their values are set in configuration files. Configure execution timeout. Etc. Provide ways to extend its functionalities by implementing cross-cuttings, custom connection string providers, or custom setting providers. Installation Install the required NuGet packages using the .NET Core CLI: dotnet add package Fanex.Data dotnet add package Fanex.Data.Repository dotnet add package Fanex.Data.SqlServer Usage Guide 1. Configure Stored Procedures in SpNames.xml Create an SpNames.xml file and add your stored procedure configurations. This file should be set to "Copy if newer" in its properties to ensure it's included in the build output. <Setting Key="QueryProducts" SpName="QueryProducts" DbName="FanexDataUnitTests"> </Setting> 2. Configure Connection Strings in appsettings.json Add your database connection strings to the appsettings.json file. "FanexConnectionStrings": [ { "Name": "FanexDataUnitTests", "ConnectionString": "Data Source=localhost;Initial Catalog=FanexDataTests;User ID=sa;Password=abczz", "ProviderName": "System.Data.SqlClient" } ] 3. Register Fanex.Data in Startup.cs or Program.cs In your Startup.cs or Program.cs, register Fanex.Data in the ConfigureServices method. services.AddFanexSql(configuration, connectionStringSection: "FanexConnectionStrings"); 4. Define a Criteria Class Create a criteria class that inherits from CriteriaBase. This class will define the parameters for your stored procedure. public class QueryProductsCriteria : CriteriaBase { public string GroupId { get; set; } public override string GetSettingKey() => "QueryProducts"; public override bool IsValid() => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(GroupId); } 5. Using DynamicRepository Instantiate DynamicRepository and use the Fetch method with your criteria object to retrieve data. var repository = new DynamicRepository(); var criteria = new QueryProductsCriteria{ GroupId = "123456" }; var products = repository.Fetch<Product>(criteria); 6. Switching Stored Procedure Versions To switch to a different version of a stored procedure (e.g., for testing), simply update the SpName attribute in your SpNames.xml file. <Setting Key="QueryProducts" SpName="QueryProducts_xtest" DbName="FanexDataUnitTests"> </Setting>

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Fanex.Data
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Installation Install the required NuGet packages using the .NET Core CLI: dotnet add package Fanex.Data dotnet add package Fanex.Data.Repository dotnet add package Fanex.Data.SqlServer Usage Guide 1. Configure Stored Procedures in SpNames.xml Create an SpNames.xml file and add your stored procedure configurations. This file should be set to "Copy if newer" in its properties to ensure it's included in the build output. <Setting Key="QueryProducts" SpName="QueryProducts" DbName="FanexDataUnitTests"> </Setting> 2. Configure Connection Strings in appsettings.json Add your database connection strings to the appsettings.json file. "FanexConnectionStrings": [ { "Name": "FanexDataUnitTests", "ConnectionString": "Data Source=localhost;Initial Catalog=FanexDataTests;User ID=sa;Password=abczz", "ProviderName": "System.Data.SqlClient" } ] 3. Register Fanex.Data in Startup.cs or Program.cs In your Startup.cs or Program.cs, register Fanex.Data in the ConfigureServices method. services.AddFanexSql(configuration, connectionStringSection: "FanexConnectionStrings"); 4. Define a Criteria Class Create a criteria class that inherits from CriteriaBase. This class will define the parameters for your stored procedure. public class QueryProductsCriteria : CriteriaBase { public string GroupId { get; set; } public override string GetSettingKey() => "QueryProducts"; public override bool IsValid() => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(GroupId); } 5. Using DynamicRepository Instantiate DynamicRepository and use the Fetch method with your criteria object to retrieve data. var repository = new DynamicRepository(); var criteria = new QueryProductsCriteria{ GroupId = "123456" }; var products = repository.Fetch<Product>(criteria); 6. Switching Stored Procedure Versions To switch to a different version of a stored procedure (e.g., for testing), simply update the SpName attribute in your SpNames.xml file. <Setting Key="QueryProducts" SpName="QueryProducts_xtest" DbName="FanexDataUnitTests"> </Setting> Back to Home

docs/introduction.html.title: Fanex.Data - A Dapper-based data access library with configurable stored procedure names. | Fanex.Data
docs/introduction.html.summary: Fanex.Data - A Dapper-based data access library with configurable stored procedure names. Packages Fanex.Data 4.3.4.5 Fanex.Data.Repository 4.3.4.5 Fanex.Data.MySql 4.3.4.5 Fanex.Data.SqlServer 4.3.4.5 Package Purposes: Fanex.Data The core library simplifies data access by leveraging Dapper. It centrally manages stored procedure names and connections through configuration files. Fanex.Data.Repository Introduces the DynamicRepository class, a simplified wrapper for Fanex.Data's ObjectDb. It provides a more straightforward interface for basic database operations, making it an ideal choice for quick and simple data access needs. Fanex.Data.MySql The MySQL-specific implementation of the Fanex.Data library Fanex.Data.SqlServer The SqlServer-specific implementation of the Fanex.Data library Features Fanex.Data is a lightweight data access library built on top of Dapper, extending its capabilities with configurable stored procedure names via an SpNames.xml file. This key feature is especially useful for managing different versions of stored procedures, allowing you to easily configure your application to call specific versions like xtest, xpre, or UAT stored procedures, even within a production environment. By centralizing the configuration of stored procedure names, Fanex.Data improves maintainability and provides a flexible solution for both SQL Server and MySQL, all while leveraging Dapper's high performance and simplicity. Key Features Execute a stored procedure returning data sets then map them to strongly typed lists. Extend ADO.Net CRUD functionalities working with stored procedures. Anonymous objects, strongly type objects, or IDictionary typed objects can be used as parameter sets to set values to stored procedure's parameters. Automatically assign values of OUTPUT parameters back to the parameter sets; which can be anonymous objects, strongly type objects, or IDictionary typed objects. Wrap any exception occurred with diagnostic information, such as: stored procedure name, parameters which are used in the execution, connection string, etc. Avoid throwing exceptions if number of values does not meet number of parameters listed in stored procedure definition. Allow developers to: Configure connection strings and connection aliases. Map between columns of result set and objects' properties. Define firm parameters, parameters which their values are set in configuration files. Configure execution timeout. Etc. Provide ways to extend its functionalities by implementing cross-cuttings, custom connection string providers, or custom setting providers.

docs/usages.html.title: ObjectDb Examples | Fanex.Data
docs/usages.html.summary: ObjectDb Examples Query Entity With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Query a single entity using an anonymous object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { OrderId = orderId, TotalOrder = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrderByIdSettingKey); var order = objectDb.QueryEntity<Order>(parameterSet); Console.WriteLine($"ShipAddress: {order.ShipAddress}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Orders: {parameterSet.TotalOrder}"); Query Entity With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Query a single entity using a Hashtable as parameter set. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { [OrderIdParameterName] = orderId, ["TotalOrder"] = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrderByIdSettingKey); var order = objectDb.QueryEntity<Order>(parameterSet); Console.WriteLine($"ShipAddress: {order.ShipAddress}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Orders: {parameterSet["TotalOrder"]}"); Query Entity With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Query a single entity using a strongly typed object as parameter set. // Arrange. var parameterSet = new OrderByIdQuery { OrderId = orderId, TotalOrder = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrderByIdSettingKey); var order = objectDb.QueryEntity<Order>(parameterSet); Console.WriteLine($"ShipAddress: {order.ShipAddress}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Orders: {parameterSet.TotalOrder}"); Query List Object With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Query a list of objects using an anonymous object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { CustomerId = TestedCustomerId, PageIndex = 1, PageSize = 10, TotalOrder = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance("QueryOrderByCustomerId"); var orders = objectDb.Query<Order>(parameterSet); Console.WriteLine($"Got {orders.Count()} of {parameterSet.TotalOrder} orders"); Query List Object With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Query a list of objects using a Hashtable as parameter set. // Arrange. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { [CustomerIdParameterName] = TestedCustomerId, ["PageIndex"] = 1, ["PageSize"] = 10, ["TotalOrder"] = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance("QueryOrderByCustomerId"); var orders = objectDb.Query<Order>(parameterSet); Console.WriteLine($"Got {orders.Count()} of {parameterSet["TotalOrder"]} orders"); Query List Object With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Query a list of objects using a strongly typed object as parameter set. // Arrange. var parameterSet = new OrdersByCustomerIdQuery { CustomerId = TestedCustomerId, PageIndex = 1, PageSize = 10, TotalOrder = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance("QueryOrderByCustomerId"); var orders = objectDb.Query<Order>(parameterSet); Console.WriteLine($"Got {orders.Count()} of {parameterSet.TotalOrder} orders"); Query Multiple With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Query multiple result sets using an anonymous object as parameter set. // Arrange. var parameterSet = new { OrderId = TestedOrderId, TotalCustomer = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrderDetailByIdSettingKey); using var multiResultReader = objectDb.QueryMultiple(parameterSet); var orders = multiResultReader.Read<Order>(); var orderDetails = multiResultReader.Read<OrderDetails>(); Console.WriteLine($"Total Customers: {parameterSet.TotalCustomer}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Orders: {orders.Count()}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Order Details: {orderDetails.Count()}"); Query Multiple With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Query multiple result sets using a Hashtable as parameter set. // Arrange. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { [OrderIdParameterName] = TestedOrderId, ["TotalCustomer"] = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrderDetailByIdSettingKey); using var multiResultReader = objectDb.QueryMultiple(parameterSet); var orders = multiResultReader.Read<Order>(); var orderDetails = multiResultReader.Read<OrderDetails>(); Console.WriteLine($"Total Customers: {parameterSet["TotalCustomer"]}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Orders: {orders.Count()}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Order Details: {orderDetails.Count()}"); Query Multiple With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Query multiple result sets using a strongly typed object as parameter set. // Arrange. var parameterSet = new OrderByIdQuery { OrderId = TestedOrderId, TotalCustomer = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrderDetailByIdSettingKey); using var multiResultReader = objectDb.QueryMultiple(parameterSet); var orders = multiResultReader.Read<Order>(); var orderDetails = multiResultReader.Read<OrderDetails>(); Console.WriteLine($"Total Customers: {parameterSet.TotalCustomer}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Orders: {orders.Count()}"); Console.WriteLine($"Total Order Details: {orderDetails.Count()}"); DataReader Examples Read One Row With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Read one row of data using an anonymous object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { OrderId = TestedOrderId, TotalOrders = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(GettingOrderByIdSettingKey); using var reader = objectDb.ExecuteReader(parameterSet); reader.Read(); var order = ReadOrder(reader); Console.WriteLine($"Ship address: {order.ShipAddress}."); Console.WriteLine($"Total orders: {parameterSet.TotalOrders}."); Read One Row With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Read one row of data using a Hashtable as parameter set. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { [OrderIdParameterName] = TestedOrderId, ["TotalOrders"] = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(GettingOrderByIdSettingKey); using var reader = objectDb.ExecuteReader(parameterSet); reader.Read(); var order = ReadOrder(reader); Console.WriteLine($"Ship address: {order.ShipAddress}."); Console.WriteLine($"Total orders: {parameterSet["TotalOrders"]}."); Read One Row With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Read one row of data using a strongly typed object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new OrderByIdQuery { OrderId = TestedOrderId, TotalOrders = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(GettingOrderByIdSettingKey); using var reader = objectDb.ExecuteReader(parameterSet); reader.Read(); var order = ReadOrder(reader); Console.WriteLine($"Ship address: {order.ShipAddress}."); Console.WriteLine($"Total orders: {parameterSet.TotalOrders}."); DataSet Examples Read DataSet With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Read data using DataSet with an anonymous object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { CustomerId = TestedCustomerId, PageIndex = 1, PageSize = 10, TotalOrders = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrdersByCustomerIdSettingKey); using var dataSet = objectDb.ExecuteDataSet(parameterSet); var dataTable = dataSet.Tables[0]; var orders = (from DataRow dataRow in dataTable.Rows select ReadOrder(dataRow)).ToList(); var totalOrders = Convert.ToInt32(parameterSet.TotalOrders); Console.WriteLine($"Got {orders.Count} of {totalOrders} orders"); Read DataSet With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Read data using DataSet with a Hashtable as parameter set. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { ["CustomerId"] = TestedCustomerId, ["PageIndex"] = 1, ["PageSize"] = 10, ["TotalOrders"] = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrdersByCustomerIdSettingKey); using var dataSet = objectDb.ExecuteDataSet(parameterSet); var dataTable = dataSet.Tables[0]; var orders = (from DataRow dataRow in dataTable.Rows select ReadOrder(dataRow)).ToList(); var totalOrders = Convert.ToInt32(parameterSet["TotalOrders"]); Console.WriteLine($"Got {orders.Count} of {totalOrders} orders"); Read DataSet With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Read data using DataSet with a strongly typed object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new OrdersByCustomerIdQuery { CustomerId = TestedCustomerId, PageIndex = 1, PageSize = 10, TotalOrders = 0 // This is an output parameter }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(QueryingOrdersByCustomerIdSettingKey); using var dataSet = objectDb.ExecuteDataSet(parameterSet); var dataTable = dataSet.Tables[0]; var orders = (from DataRow dataRow in dataTable.Rows select ReadOrder(dataRow)).ToList(); var totalOrders = Convert.ToInt32(parameterSet.TotalOrders); Console.WriteLine($"Got {orders.Count} of {totalOrders} orders"); ExecuteNonQuery Examples Execute Non Query With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Execute a non-query operation using an anonymous object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { EmployeeId = TestedEmployeeId, TerritoryId = 0 }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance("InsertEmployeeTerritory"); var effectedRows = objectDb.ExecuteNonQuery(parameterSet); // TerritoryId is an output parameter var territoryId = parameterSet.TerritoryId; Console.WriteLine(territoryId); Console.WriteLine(effectedRows); Execute Non Query With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Execute a non-query operation using a Hashtable as parameter set. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { ["EmployeeId"] = TestedEmployeeId, ["TerritoryId"] = TestedTerritoryId }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance("InsertEmployeeTerritory"); var effectedRows = objectDb.ExecuteNonQuery(parameterSet); // TerritoryId is an output parameter var territoryId = parameterSet["TerritoryId"]; Console.WriteLine(territoryId); Console.WriteLine(effectedRows); Execute Non Query With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Execute a non-query operation using a strongly typed object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { EmployeeId = TestedEmployeeId, TerritoryId = TestedTerritoryId }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance("InsertEmployeeTerritory"); var effectedRows = objectDb.ExecuteNonQuery(parameterSet); // TerritoryId is an output parameter var territoryId = parameterSet.TerritoryId; Console.WriteLine(territoryId); Console.WriteLine(effectedRows); ExecuteScalar Examples Execute Scalar With Parameter Set Being An Anonymous Object Execute a scalar operation using an anonymous object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new { ProductId = TestedProductId, ProductName = string.Empty }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(CountingProductsSettingKey); var orderCount = Convert.ToInt32(objectDb.ExecuteScalar(parameterSet)); // ProductName is an output parameter var productName = parameterSet.ProductName; Console.WriteLine(orderCount); Console.WriteLine(productName); Execute Scalar With Parameter Set Being A Hashtable Execute a scalar operation using a Hashtable as parameter set. var parameterSet = new Hashtable(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { ["ProductId"] = TestedProductId, ["ProductName"] = string.Empty }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(CountingProductsSettingKey); var orderCount = Convert.ToInt32(objectDb.ExecuteScalar(parameterSet)); // ProductName is an output parameter var productName = parameterSet["ProductName"]; Console.WriteLine(orderCount); Console.WriteLine(productName); Execute Scalar With Parameter Set Being A Strongly Typed Object Execute a scalar operation using a strongly typed object as parameter set. var parameterSet = new OrderCountByProductIdQuery { ProductId = TestedProductId }; using var objectDb = ObjectDbFactory.CreateInstance(CountingProductsSettingKey); var orderCount = Convert.ToInt32(objectDb.ExecuteScalar(parameterSet)); // ProductName is an output parameter var productName = parameterSet.ProductName; Console.WriteLine(orderCount); Console.WriteLine(productName); Back to Home
